questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Brisbane, Australia, as I wanted to be somewhere with amazing nature, weather, people and with a lot of things to experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience was amazing! I would recommend it to everybody. You get amazing friends for life that you're able to go on trips around Australia with every weekend, and experience so many things with all the time. UQ was a really good uni, which was an added bonus.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UQ had sent a lot of emails beforehand with a lot of information, and a lot was available on their website as well. The first week of uni there is called Orientation Week, which is a week dedicated to introducing new students and exchange students to the uni.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During Orientation Week there are a lot of different lectures and stuff you can go to to get information on things, get guided tours around the uni, and meet other students. Here you can ask any questions you may have as well

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I had no trouble

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at a student accommodation called Westella, and I would highly recommend it! You live with 21 other exchange students and share 4 kitchens and bathrooms. You become really close friends with the people here, and they will be like your second family on exchange. Westella was also half the price of other student accommodations, and the location was amazing. I booked my room in April and got one of the last ones. I've heard from other people who don't live at Westella, that it was a bit difficult finding affordable housing here. Other student accomodations include StudentOne, Scape and Unilodge. Some people also found private housing through Flatmates. If you are in contact with any other students from UCPH going to Brisbane, I would recommend looking for something with them!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I recommend living off campus, as you are closer to all the popular neighbourhoods in Brisbane - West End, South Bank, CBD, Kangaroo Point, Fortitude Valley. It is mainly Australian students who live at the colleges on campus, and they are in general a bit younger than Danish students - in Australia they start uni at 17 or 18 years old. But if you want to become friends with locals its a great place to live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It can be pretty expensive unfortunately:( Start looking early

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No problem

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as being pretty easy. UCPH helped, and UQ sent a detailed email about what you have to do, which was just send you placement to UQ from UCPH, your proof of english proficiency, and probably one other document.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both UQ and UCPH were easy to get in contact with over mail if you had any questions! I had no troubles.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted on the first try. I think the official registration was around end June/early July. The only thing was that the courses you take have to be approved for exchange students. So if it doesn't specify on the course description that its approved for exchange students, you have to write the UQ exchange student coordinator to hear if the course can get approved. UQ also has a list on their webpage with courses that are pre-approved for exchange students, you can browse through

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the beginning of June UQ opened up a timetable feature on their webpage, where you could see what time of the week lectures for the different courses were. I recommend choosing courses where you get Fridays off, so you can go on weekend trips!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ended up spending only a little bit less time on school here compared to at UCPH, but it depends a lot on which courses you take.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the 3rd year courses here were about the same as 3rd year courses in Denmark. The teachers were really good, sweet and helpful.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is different from UCPH in the sense that they have multiple assessments throughout the semester here that count towards your grade and not only a final exam. There were things like assignments, quizzes, presentations, and midterms. All the lectures here were also recorded, which meant that very few people showed up to the lectures. Lab (practical classes) were however mandatory, so this is were I met most of my friends in my courses. Also, all exams in science courses here are closed book.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Molecular Cell Biology II (BIOL3006), Microbial Genomics (MICR3004), Evolution (BIOL2201), and Living Ocean (MARS1001)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I'm satisfied with all four courses that I took. They were all interesting and had great teachers, but could also be pretty time consuming at times. Molecular Cell Biology and Living Oceans were probably my favourites, as they were really interesting. In Evolution and Living Oceans I learnt about Australian nature and marine life, which I thought was really cool.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some unexpected costs were the mandatory Australian Health Insurance (OSHC) which cost 1700 kr, and the Australian student visa which was 6650 kr. I can also add to this budget that I spend about 2200 kr per month on travelling.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport in Queensland is only 50 cents! Alcohol was pretty expensive though. Overall, you have to be prepared for things to be expensive in Australia.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UQ has a lot of amazing clubs, and this is the main way that students in Australia get friends, so I definitely recommend joining some!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a club or exchange students (QUEST), and they also have a lot of sport clubs incl. surfing, hiking, and diving. They also have all other kinds of cultural clubs and clubs for different degrees.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I definitely recommend QUEST! Every exchange student (even some from QUT) are in this club, and they do pub nights every Thursday, weekend trips to Noosa, Byron Bay and Moreton Island, and pub crawl parties. I would also recommend the UniDive club - I got my diving certificate here with some other exchange students, and it was amazing. The surf club was also good. Be prepared to sign up early for club events, as the tickets sell out fast!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
In Brisbane: Felons, West End Market, BBQ at Kangaroo Point
Weekend trips: North Stradbroke Island, Moreton Island, Gold Coast, Springbrooke, Byron Bay, Noosa, Sunshine Coast, Rainbow Coast, K'agri, and much more! During the mid-semester break I recommend going on a roadtrip in Northern Queensland

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it's similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join club! And talk to them in classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The only one I had trouble getting used to was having to walk on the left side of the street.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very social, open and kind. Talk to the locals, they love giving recommendations.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do it! It is going to be the most amazing time of your life, so I definitely recommend going!
2. The time difference is going to be pretty difficult, and when you're busy down here on exchange it's going to be difficult staying in touch with people back at home
3. Talk to the other exchange students as much as you can. They are going to be your friends down here, and make your semester so special

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm glad I chose Brisbane and not Sydney or Melbourne, as the weather is so much better here, and you get to go on so many weekend trips all over the east coast. It is a bit far away from the nearest beach tho (1,5 hours), but trains to Gold Coast is only $0,5

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends you make for life while on exchange. I also really loved being able to be in nature all the time, whether that was hiking or going to the beach, and seeing amazing animals everywhere. Living in another country and experiencing a new culture is also just amazing in itself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not seeing my family for 5 months

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It's going to be pretty expensive, but applying for grants (legater) will definitely be worth it. It was however more difficult getting grants as a bachelor's student than I thought it would be.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
